_comment: The How to play guide: one page per entry, in order. 'picture' is a building id shown above the text.

pages.title: Welcome to Brume
pages.body:
Your colony owes the Harrow & Vell Charter Company for the trip here. Payments start on turn 30 and come due every 10 turns, each a bit bigger. Pay off the whole debt and the colony is yours. Miss three payments in a row and the Company takes over. If everyone dies, the colony goes silent.

Each turn you build, then press End turn. Take your time: nothing happens until you end the turn.

pages.title: Building
pages.body:
Choose a building (the list on the left, or Build on a phone), then tap a tile. Green means you can build there, red means you can't; the hint at the bottom says why.

Buildings join only through their doors (shown in orange while you place one): hubs like the Bunkhouse have 4, workplaces 2 (in one side, out the other), and outlying machines 1. A new building needs a door facing a door or a Heat Main next to it; press R or Rotate to turn it. Heat Mains (1 alloy each) join on every side, so lay them to reach further out and to give buildings somewhere to plug in.

Drag the map to move it, and pinch, use the mouse wheel or the - and + buttons to zoom. Dragging never builds.

pages.title: Power and heat
pages.body:
Every building needs workers, and most need power and heat.

Mirror Fields make power from sunlight: weak on the cold night side (west), strong on the hot day side (east). Vent Taps sit on orange vents and give lots of heat. Buildings need more heat the further west they are.

If there isn't enough, some buildings sit idle and show a red dot. Select one to see why.

pages.title: Keeping people alive
pages.body:
Everyone eats, breathes and drinks every turn.

Ice Drills sit on ice and make water. Splitters turn water into oxygen. Kelp Vats turn water into food.

If food, oxygen or water runs out, people die, and oxygen runs out fastest. Keep an eye on the numbers at the top: red means a shortage.

pages.title: Homes and morale
pages.body:
Bunkhouses give people somewhere to live. Overcrowding makes people sick and unhappy.

Morale sets how hard everyone works. The Commons, Clinic, Lounge and Garden Cavern raise it; shortages, crowding, waste and missed payments lower it. Below 20, people walk out.

The Clinic also halves deaths from illness and old age.

pages.title: Making money
pages.body:
Seam Cutters sit on teal ore seams and cut ore. Forges smelt ore into alloy, which is also what you build with.

Spin Launchers sell alloy to orbit for marks, the money you pay the Company with. They never sell below your export reserve (set it in Company account), so you keep enough alloy to build.

You can pay the debt early from Company account.

pages.title: Going underground
pages.body:
A Shaft opens the Deep, a level under the surface. Switch levels with Surface and Deep (or Q and E).

Open caverns cost the normal price. Solid rock must be dug out first: it costs more alloy and takes longer, unless you own a Borer drone. Ore veins are richer than surface seams, deep vents give more heat, and Ice Drills work on underground water.

Icequakes never reach the Deep.

pages.title: Research and trouble
pages.body:
Survey Labs make research toward the topic you choose. Finished topics make buildings better and unlock new ones.

Machines break down now and then; Workshops fix them faster. Crime grows with crowding and low morale; Warden Posts hold it down. A plague can break out in a big colony, and your labs must find a cure in time.

The Company and the Crews' Union both watch how you run things, and story events will ask you to choose.

pages.title: Drones and orbit
pages.body:
A Fab Shop turns alloy into parts. Parts build drones, satellites and the biggest buildings.

A Drone Bay runs work drones: Graders build faster on the surface, Borers dig faster below, Prospectors find loose ore and Haulers speed up Seam Cutters. You'll see them working on the map.

A working Spin Launcher can launch satellites: weather (less storm damage), relay (morale) and power (for Beam Catchers). Use the Drones & orbit button.

pages.title: Tips
pages.body:
Colony report shows where power, heat and workers go, what changed last turn, and which buildings are idle and why.

Run 5 turns skips ahead, and stops if something needs your choice.

The game saves itself every 10 turns; Save keeps your own copy. On the title screen, Leaderboard shows how others did.

Good luck, and keep the air on.
